title: Exploring gender-based violence experiences of LGBTQIA+ migrant youth in Canada
abstract: LGBTQIA+ migrants face elevated risks of gender-based violence (GBV) across migration contexts, yet limited research has focused on youth or examined how experiences of violence vary within this population in Canada. This exploratory study examines the forms of violence experienced by LGBTQIA+ migrant youth aged 15–24 in Canada, as well as variation across demographic characteristics. Survey data were collected in 2024 through a national, community-based research project using online recruitment via newcomer- and LGBTQIA+-serving organisations. The final analytic sample included 85 LGBTQIA+ migrant youth. Measures assessed multiple forms of violence, including physical, sexual, emotional, stalking and online abuse, alongside key demographic variables. Descriptive and bivariate analyses were conducted. Overall, findings indicate that LGBTQIA+ migrant youth experience high levels of multidimensional violence, with many reporting exposure to more than one form of abuse. Patterns across demographic characteristics suggest that experiences of violence are shaped by intersecting identities related to gender, sexuality, migration status and region of origin, underscoring the heterogeneity of risk within this population. This study contributes initial quantitative evidence on GBV among LGBTQIA+ migrant youth in Canada, highlighting the need for policies, prevention strategies and service responses that address violence affecting this population.
